dockerfile
# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package management
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI, git, wget, and certificates
# This is done in a single RUN command to reduce layer count.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set a working directory for the build process
WORKDIR /build

# Build and install all dependencies (Metis, Hypre, MFEM) and the application (Laghos) from source
# This is a single, long RUN command to keep the image layers to a minimum, as per best practices
# without using a multi-stage build.
RUN \
    #
    # --- Build and Install Metis 4.0.3 ---
    #
    echo "Building METIS..." && \
    wget https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    # Build the library with the specified OPTFLAGS to avoid build errors on modern compilers
    make lib "OPTFLAGS=-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    # Manually install the library and header to a system location
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    #
    # --- Build and Install Hypre 2.28.0 ---
    #
    echo "Building HYPRE..." && \
    wget https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v2.28.0.tar.gz -O hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    # Configure with MPI compilers and specified flags
    ./configure CC=mpicc CXX=mpicxx --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    \
    #
    # --- Build MFEM 4.7 ---
    #
    echo "Building MFEM..." && \
    git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    git checkout v4.7 && \
    # Build the parallel version, pointing to the previously installed dependencies
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local METIS_DIR=/usr/local && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    #
    # --- Build Laghos ---
    #
    echo "Building Laghos..." && \
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    # Build the application, pointing to the MFEM source directory
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=../mfem && \
    # Copy the final executable to a system location on the PATH
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    cd ..

# Set the final working directory for the application runtime
WORKDIR /app

# Copy the required data files from the Laghos source into the runtime WORKDIR,
# clean up the build directory to reduce image size, and update the linker cache.
RUN cp /build/Laghos/data/* . \
    && rm -rf /build \
    && ldconfig

# The entrypoint/command would be set at runtime, e.g., using 'mpirun -np 4 laghos ...'

# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package management
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI, git, wget, and certificates
# This is done in a single RUN command to reduce layer count.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set a working directory for the build process
WORKDIR /build

# Build and install all dependencies (Metis, Hypre, MFEM) and the application (Laghos) from source
# This is a single, long RUN command to keep the image layers to a minimum, as per best practices
# without using a multi-stage build.
RUN \
    #
    # --- Build and Install Metis 4.0.3 ---
    #
    echo "Building METIS..." && \
    wget https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    # FIX: Corrected make command. Removed invalid 'lib' target and used proper syntax for OPTFLAGS.
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    # Manually install the library and header to a system location
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    #
    # --- Build and Install Hypre 2.28.0 ---
    #
    echo "Building HYPRE..." && \
    wget https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v2.28.0.tar.gz -O hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    # Configure with MPI compilers and specified flags
    ./configure CC=mpicc CXX=mpicxx --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    \
    #
    # --- Build MFEM 4.7 ---
    #
    echo "Building MFEM..." && \
    git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    git checkout v4.7 && \
    # Build the parallel version, pointing to the previously installed dependencies
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local METIS_DIR=/usr/local && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    #
    # --- Build Laghos ---
    #
    echo "Building Laghos..." && \
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    # Build the application, pointing to the MFEM source directory
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=../mfem && \
    # Copy the final executable to a system location on the PATH
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    cd ..

# Set the final working directory for the application runtime
WORKDIR /app

# Copy the required data files from the Laghos source into the runtime WORKDIR,
# clean up the build directory to reduce image size, and update the linker cache.
RUN cp /build/Laghos/data/* . \
    && rm -rf /build \
    && ldconfig

# The entrypoint/command would be set at runtime, e.g., using 'mpirun -np 4 laghos ...'

# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package management
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI, git, wget, and certificates
# This is done in a single RUN command to reduce layer count.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set a working directory for the build process
WORKDIR /build

# Build and install all dependencies (Metis, Hypre, MFEM) and the application (Laghos) from source
# This is a single, long RUN command to keep the image layers to a minimum, as per best practices
# without using a multi-stage build.
RUN \
    #
    # --- Build and Install Metis 4.0.3 ---
    #
    echo "Building METIS..." && \
    wget https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    # FIX: Corrected copy paths. METIS 4.0.3 places build artifacts in the 'Lib' subdirectory.
    cp Lib/libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    #
    # --- Build and Install Hypre 2.28.0 ---
    #
    echo "Building HYPRE..." && \
    wget https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v2.28.0.tar.gz -O hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    # Configure with MPI compilers and specified flags
    ./configure CC=mpicc CXX=mpicxx --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    \
    #
    # --- Build MFEM 4.7 ---
    #
    echo "Building MFEM..." && \
    git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    git checkout v4.7 && \
    # Build the parallel version, pointing to the previously installed dependencies
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local METIS_DIR=/usr/local && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    #
    # --- Build Laghos ---
    #
    echo "Building Laghos..." && \
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    # Build the application, pointing to the MFEM source directory
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=../mfem && \
    # Copy the final executable to a system location on the PATH
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    cd ..

# Set the final working directory for the application runtime
WORKDIR /app

# Copy the required data files from the Laghos source into the runtime WORKDIR,
# clean up the build directory to reduce image size, and update the linker cache.
RUN cp /build/Laghos/data/* . \
    && rm -rf /build \
    && ldconfig

# The entrypoint/command would be set at runtime, e.g., using 'mpirun -np 4 laghos ...'

# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package management
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI, git, wget, and certificates
# This is done in a single RUN command to reduce layer count.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set a working directory for the build process
WORKDIR /build

# Build and install all dependencies (Metis, Hypre, MFEM) and the application (Laghos) from source
# This is a single, long RUN command to keep the image layers to a minimum, as per best practices
# without using a multi-stage build.
RUN \
    #
    # --- Build and Install Metis 4.0.3 ---
    #
    echo "Building METIS..." && \
    wget https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    # FIX: Corrected paths. The library is in the source root, but the header is in the 'Lib' subdirectory.
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    #
    # --- Build and Install Hypre 2.28.0 ---
    #
    echo "Building HYPRE..." && \
    wget https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v2.28.0.tar.gz -O hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    # Configure with MPI compilers and specified flags
    ./configure CC=mpicc CXX=mpicxx --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    \
    #
    # --- Build MFEM 4.7 ---
    #
    echo "Building MFEM..." && \
    git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    git checkout v4.7 && \
    # Build the parallel version, pointing to the previously installed dependencies
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local METIS_DIR=/usr/local && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    #
    # --- Build Laghos ---
    #
    echo "Building Laghos..." && \
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    # Build the application, pointing to the MFEM source directory
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=../mfem && \
    # Copy the final executable to a system location on the PATH
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    cd ..

# Set the final working directory for the application runtime
WORKDIR /app

# Copy the required data files from the Laghos source into the runtime WORKDIR,
# clean up the build directory to reduce image size, and update the linker cache.
RUN cp /build/Laghos/data/* . \
    && rm -rf /build \
    && ldconfig

# The entrypoint/command would be set at runtime, e.g., using 'mpirun -np 4 laghos ...'

# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package management
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI, git, wget, and certificates
# This is done in a single RUN command to reduce layer count.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set a working directory for the build process
WORKDIR /build

# Build and install all dependencies (Metis, Hypre, MFEM) and the application (Laghos) from source
# This is a single, long RUN command to keep the image layers to a minimum, as per best practices
# without using a multi-stage build.
RUN \
    #
    # --- Build and Install Metis 4.0.3 ---
    #
    echo "Building METIS..." && \
    wget https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    # FIX: Corrected compiler flag syntax for METIS build (-Wno-error=... instead of -Wno-error-...).
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    # The library is in the source root, but the header is in the 'Lib' subdirectory.
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    #
    # --- Build and Install Hypre 2.28.0 ---
    #
    echo "Building HYPRE..." && \
    wget https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v2.28.0.tar.gz -O hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    # Configure with MPI compilers and specified flags
    ./configure CC=mpicc CXX=mpicxx --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    # MFEM requires HYPRE_config.h, which is not installed by default. Copy it manually.
    cp HYPRE_config.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd ../.. && \
    \
    #
    # --- Build MFEM 4.7 ---
    #
    echo "Building MFEM..." && \
    git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    git checkout v4.7 && \
    # Build the parallel version, pointing to the previously installed dependencies
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local METIS_DIR=/usr/local && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    #
    # --- Build Laghos ---
    #
    echo "Building Laghos..." && \
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    # Build the application, pointing to the MFEM source directory
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=../mfem && \
    # Copy the final executable to a system location on the PATH
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    cd ..

# Set the final working directory for the application runtime
WORKDIR /app

# Copy the required data files from the Laghos source into the runtime WORKDIR,
# clean up the build directory to reduce image size, and update the linker cache.
RUN cp /build/Laghos/data/* . \
    && rm -rf /build \
    && ldconfig

# The entrypoint/command would be set at runtime, e.g., using 'mpirun -np 4 laghos ...'

# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package management
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI, git, wget, and certificates
# This is done in a single RUN command to reduce layer count.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set a working directory for the build process
WORKDIR /build

# Build and install all dependencies (Metis, Hypre, MFEM) and the application (Laghos) from source
# This is a single, long RUN command to keep the image layers to a minimum, as per best practices
# without using a multi-stage build.
RUN \
    #
    # --- Build and Install Metis 4.0.3 ---
    #
    echo "Building METIS..." && \
    wget https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    # The library is in the source root, but the header is in the 'Lib' subdirectory.
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    #
    # --- Build and Install Hypre 2.28.0 ---
    #
    echo "Building HYPRE..." && \
    wget https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v2.28.0.tar.gz -O hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    # Configure with MPI compilers and specified flags
    ./configure CC=mpicc CXX=mpicxx --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    # FIX: The HYPRE 'make install' is incomplete. Copy headers and the static library manually.
    cp HYPRE_config.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cp hypre/include/*.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cp lib/libHYPRE.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cd ../.. && \
    \
    #
    # --- Build MFEM 4.7 ---
    #
    echo "Building MFEM..." && \
    git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    git checkout v4.7 && \
    # Build the parallel version, pointing to the previously installed dependencies
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local METIS_DIR=/usr/local && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    #
    # --- Build Laghos ---
    #
    echo "Building Laghos..." && \
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    # Build the application, pointing to the MFEM source directory
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=../mfem && \
    # Copy the final executable to a system location on the PATH
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    cd ..

# Set the final working directory for the application runtime
WORKDIR /app

# Copy the required data files from the Laghos source into the runtime WORKDIR,
# clean up the build directory to reduce image size, and update the linker cache.
RUN cp /build/Laghos/data/* . \
    && rm -rf /build \
    && ldconfig

# The entrypoint/command would be set at runtime, e.g., using 'mpirun -np 4 laghos ...'

flux-minicluster-manifest
# This manifest incorporates the provided debugging analysis to fix the "unsatisfiable request" error.
# It targets a specific, larger AWS instance type and scales the job to use all available cores.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for the optimized MiniCluster job.
  name: laghos-cpu-aws-optimized
  # Deploying to the default namespace as requested.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods in the MiniCluster. Set to 1 for a single-node run.
  size: 1

  # Increase tasks to 64 to fully utilize the vCPUs of the selected hpc7g.16xlarge instance.
  tasks: 64

  # Do not delete the job pods and services upon completion for debugging.
  cleanup: false

  # Flux Operator logging settings. Strict mode ensures all logs are captured.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Pod spec to control scheduling and ensure the job lands on a node with sufficient resources.
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      # Selects an AWS Graviton (ARM64) instance with 64 vCPUs, resolving the resource issue.
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge

  # Flux spec to configure the Flux Framework itself.
  flux:
    container:
      # Use the ARM64-compatible flux-view image, which is required for Graviton instances.
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # Define the single container that will run the HPC application.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:laghos

      # The updated application command with performance tuning flags.
      # '-p 3' uses a higher-order polynomial and '-pa' enables partial assembly.
      command: laghos -p 3 -pa -m cube_311_hex.mesh

      # Per explicit original instructions, launcher must be false under all circumstances.
      # The application command will run in the main container of the broker pod (pod-0).
      launcher: false

Optimization Decisions

Decision 1: RETRY

Agent's Rationale: The initial run on a 64-core ARM instance provides a strong baseline. This attempt switches to a high-performance 48 vCPU x86 instance (c7a.12xlarge) and maps tasks to its 24 physical cores. This strategy aims to improve performance by avoiding SMT/hyper-threading contention, which can be detrimental for CPU- and memory-bound HPC workloads.

Decision 2: STOP

Agent's Rationale: The initial run on the ARM-based hpc7g.16xlarge instance with 64 tasks achieved the highest performance (127.9). The subsequent attempt on a c7a.12xlarge x86 instance with 24 tasks (matching physical cores) yielded a lower score (124.5). This indicates that for this specific workload, either the higher core count or the Graviton3 architecture provides a significant advantage over the tested x86 configurations. Further tuning of x86 instances is unlikely to surpass the initial result. Therefore, the optimal configuration found is the first one.
